reviews.rationale: Sequential comparison of selected GAAP quarterly rows shows net interest income and pretax and net income to common rising, with total interest income up and total interest expense slightly down, while noninterest income fell and noninterest expense was essentially flat. The noninterest income decline is directionally consistent with the collapse of the net gain on sale or write-down of assets line, but the selected rows do not decompose the remaining noninterest income components, so the driver is unresolved rather than established. Credit indicators moved adversely on a sequential basis: nonaccrual and nonperforming loans rose, other real estate and total nonperforming assets rose, the residential and consumer/other nonperforming components increased while commercial real estate declined, net charge-offs and the annualized net charge-off ratio increased, the nonperforming-asset ratio rose, and the allowance balance and allowance coverage ratio declined. Period-end loans fell while deposits rose. These are point-in-time and single-quarter company-reported measures on differing bases, so they are not a causal explanation and not a year-over-year trend. The earnings improvement and the credit deterioration point in opposite directions, and the selected extract lacks allowance provisioning, reserve-build or release detail, loan-mix and yield/cost decomposition, noninterest income components, capital and liquidity measures, and any management guidance or company-defined non-GAAP reconciliation. Because the evidence is mixed and the causal drivers are unresolved, the research state is held for review rather than upgraded or invalidated; conviction and status are preserved and the thesis remains blocked from downstream decisions pending a complete, conflict-free source set for the same period.
